owner: FIX_MOVE_FOR_CHARGE (movement: end the move inside realistic charge reach of the melee target — OFF-02/OFF-11/OFF-12)
rationale: 11e 11.02 / 11.04: a charge is declared, then 2D6 is rolled, and only an enemy unit within 12" AND within that roll — measured base to base, engagement range does not extend it (11.04 example B; errata FAQ under 02.02: modifiers count, and a charge roll is never more than 12) — can be selected as a charge target. So the Normal move before the charge decides what roll the charge will need, and that is set by the edge gap between the closest pair of models, not by the centroids. Here U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B (5 x 40 mm, M6, guardian spears S7 A5 AP-2 D2 in melee: melee-focused) stands in a line 65 px apart at y 650, 15.8" centroid to centroid and 10.2" edge to edge from U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_C_P2, a wide line 140 px apart at y 1120 — the nearest enemy, so the melee chase gate makes it ATTACK it with a Normal move (15.8 - 6 <= 12; Custodes have no advance-and-charge, and an Advance forfeits the charge, 09.06). The flag-off attack move aims the whole 0.95 x M step (228 px) at the target's centroid and ends 5.9" from its nearest model: a 6+ to charge, 26/36 = 72%. Aiming the same step from the squad's closest model at the target's nearest model ends 4.5" away: a 5+, 30/36 = 83% — the best the move allows (10.2" - 5.7"). The asserts grade the board as the Movement phase left it (setup stashes it when the phase completes; the runner lets the AI shoot and charge before grading) and count every positioned model, so a model lost to Fire Overwatch cannot move a number. Assert 1 pins the flag-off geometry on the engine's own distances, so the exam cannot drift into passing by layout; asserts 3-7 stop a pass by an illegal move (ending in engagement range, 09.05), by doing nothing, by over-moving, by an Advance, or by dropping the announced ATTACK.
